meta.rule_version: Labor Code of the Philippines / PD 851 / DOLE Handbook on Workers' Statutory Monetary Benefits

half_month_causes: Closure or cessation of operations not due to serious losses or financial reverses
Disease not curable within six months where continued employment is prejudicial to health
Lack of service assignment of a security guard for a continuous six months
Lack of service assignment of a contractor's/subcontractor's worker for a continuous three months
one_month_causes: Impossible reinstatement for reasons not attributable to the employer
Lack of service assignment of a security guard by reason of age
separation_pay.source_note: Labor Code Arts. 298–299 as summarised in the DOLE Handbook on Workers' Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024, Ch. 14 (½-month vs one-month causes; minimum one month; latest salary rate incl. regular allowances; tax-exempt under NIRC Sec. 32(B)(6)(b))

retirement_pay.source_note: Labor Code Art. 302 (RA 7641) as summarised in the DOLE Handbook 2024, Ch. 15: ½-month salary per year of service = 22.5 days (15 days + 5 days SIL + 1/12 of 13th month); age 60–65 with ≥5 years' service; not applicable to retail/service/agricultural establishments with ≤10 employees; COLA excluded

sil_exclusions: Government employees, including those of GOCCs with original charters
Persons in the personal service of another
Managerial employees (manage the establishment or a department, regularly direct two or more employees, and can hire or fire or effectively recommend it)
Officers or members of a managerial staff meeting the Handbook's four conditions
Field personnel and others whose time and performance are unsupervised
Those with vacation leave with pay of at least five days
Those in establishments regularly employing fewer than ten employees

types.name: Service Incentive Leave
types.conditions: At least one year of service, continuous or broken, within 12 months
types.cash: Yes: unused SIL is converted to cash at year-end or on resignation, at the current daily rate, pro rata

types.name: Maternity Leave
types.duration: 105 days with full pay (120 days for a qualified solo parent); 60 days for miscarriage or emergency termination of pregnancy; optional extra 30 days without pay
types.conditions: At least three monthly SSS contributions in the 12 months before the semester of childbirth, and notice of the pregnancy to the employer
types.cash: Paid as SSS maternity benefit plus the employer's salary differential; up to 7 days may be allocated to the child's father

types.name: Paternity Leave
types.duration: 7 days with full pay per delivery, for the first four deliveries
types.conditions: Married, cohabiting with the wife, and applied within a reasonable time (no prior application needed for a miscarriage)
types.cash: No: not convertible to cash if unused

types.name: Parental Leave for Solo Parents
types.duration: Up to 7 working days with pay every year
types.conditions: At least six months of service, notice to the employer, and a valid Solo Parent ID (SPIC) from the city or municipal social welfare office
types.cash: No, unless agreed with the employer; not cumulative

types.name: Leave for Victims of VAWC
types.duration: Up to 10 days with full pay, extendable as the protection order requires
types.conditions: Certification from the punong barangay or kagawad, prosecutor or Clerk of Court that a VAWC action is pending
types.cash: No: not convertible and not cumulative

types.name: Special Leave for Women
types.duration: Up to 2 months (60 calendar days) a year with full pay, per the physician's certified recuperation period
types.conditions: Six months' continuous aggregate service in the 12 months before surgery for a gynecological disorder, and an application within a reasonable time

leave.source_note: DOLE Handbook on Workers' Statutory Monetary Benefits, 2024 Edition: summary table of statutory leave benefits and Chapters 7 (SIL, Art. 95, with the ₱610 example), 8 (maternity, RA 11210), 9 (paternity, RA 8187), 10 (solo parents, RA 11861), 11 (VAWC, RA 9262) and 12 (special leave for women, RA 9710).
